note: Constants for the forming simulator (scripts/forming.js). Viscosity is not here: it is the NBS 710 Fulcher fit in viscosity.json. Every value is either sourced (source key) or marked assumed; assumed values are typical figures chosen for the model, not measurements of this glass.

conductivity.units: W/(m·K), k = a + b·T with T in °C
conductivity.note: Phononic (true) conductivity of soda-lime-silica melts, fitted from 1100 to 1550 °C and independent of iron content. Used here below 1100 °C too; their reference for solid float glass, 1.14 + 6.24e-4·T from 240 to 500 °C, is within 0.2 W/(m·K) of it over that range.

source.label: Liu, Kitamura, Xia and Pilon, Conductive and radiative properties of soda-lime silicate glassmelts with different iron contents from 1100 °C to 1500 °C, J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 99 (2016) 1271, eq. 14

absorption.note: Two-band absorption coefficients (1/m) from the same paper: band 1 is 0–2.8 µm and depends on iron, band 2 is 2.8–5 µm and does not; beyond 5 µm the melt is opaque (κ above 5000 1/m). Refractive index 1.49 throughout.

surface.note: Fraction of radiation that crosses the surface rather than reflecting, about 1 minus the hemispherical reflectance for n ≈ 1.5 (assumed; normal-incidence reflectance is 4%).

heatCapacity.note: Assumed, held constant: typical of soda-lime melts above the glass transition (unverified). Room-temperature glass is nearer 840.

surfaceTension.note: Typical of soda-lime melts near working heat (unverified).

convection.note: Assumed natural-convection coefficient for a gather turning in still shop air.

breath.note: Assumed range for a blower's sustained mouth pressure, and an assumed most they can exhale (flow, litres per second) while holding it; not measured. Adults can push roughly 10 kPa at maximum effort (unverified).

gather.note: A first gather about 7 cm across, on a pipe whose bore leaves a 3 mm pocket of air at the tip (assumed sizes).
